findings.title: 2FA users without backup codes have no way to obtain them
findings.body: Any user who enabled 2FA before this PR has `backupCodes = NULL`. If they click "Lost access" and try to log in with a backup code, `authorize` throws `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes`, and the login UI shows the message "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." However there is no way to (re)generate backup codes once 2FA is already enabled: `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` returns `TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled` when `user.twoFactorEnabled` is true. These existing users therefore hit a permanent dead end, and the guidance in the message is false. A regeneration path (or disabling/re-enabling) is needed before this is safe to ship.

findings.title: Dismissing dialog after enable skips onEnable()
findings.body: Previously `handleEnable` called `onEnable()` immediately on success. Now it only advances to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`, and `onEnable()` is called solely from the "Close" button. If the user enables 2FA and then dismisses the dialog via the X button, overlay click, or Escape (`onOpenChange`), `onEnable()` is never invoked and `resetState()` never runs. The parent settings page is not notified that 2FA is now enabled, so the two-factor switch stays visually off while the account actually has 2FA active. The `onOpenChange` handler should invoke `onEnable()` when the flow had reached the post-enable backup-code step (and reset state).

findings.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: Consuming a backup code does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes))`, finds the index, sets `backupCodes[index] = null`, then writes the whole re-encrypted array back. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both read the pre-consumption array, both find the code, and both write — resulting in the code being accepted twice (and the two writes clobbering each other). Since the guaranteed single-use property is the core security promise of backup codes, this should be made atomic (e.g., a conditional update / transaction) rather than a read-then-write.

findings.title: No test coverage for backup code login or one-time consumption
findings.body: The added e2e work only asserts that the download/copy/close buttons appear on the backup-code screen (with `// TODO: check file content` and `// TODO: check clipboard content`), and the header even notes `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup`. The core new behavior — logging in with a backup code via "Lost access", the one-time deletion of the consumed code, `MissingBackupCodes`/`IncorrectBackupCode` handling, and disabling 2FA with a backup code — is entirely untested. The PR checklist itself states "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective." The most bug-prone logic (code consumption/concurrency) is unverified.

findings.title: Copy success toast shown without awaiting clipboard write
findings.body: `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` returns a promise that is neither awaited nor caught, and the "backup codes copied!" success toast is fired unconditionally. In non-secure contexts or when clipboard permission is denied the write rejects silently while the user is told the copy succeeded — dangerous here because backup codes are shown once. The toast (and the e2e assertion on `toast-success`) should only fire after the write resolves.

findings.title: Backup-codes object URL is never revoked on unmount
findings.body: `setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))` creates an object URL that is only revoked on a subsequent `handleSetup` call. If the user closes the dialog (or the component unmounts) the blob URL leaks. The URL should be revoked in a cleanup effect on unmount.

findings.title: tabIndex={-1} makes password visibility toggle keyboard-inaccessible for all PasswordFields
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the show/hide-password button removes it from the tab order for every `PasswordField` in the app, not just the two-factor modals this PR targets. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the toggle, which is an accessibility regression. If the intent was only to prevent a specific form-submit issue, it should be scoped rather than applied to the shared component.
